metadata.subject: CPL/ATPL Aviation Meteorology

questions.question: Lowest layer of atmosphere is
questions.explanation: Troposphere is the lowest portion of the atmosphere extending from surface to 16-18 km at equator and 8-10 km at poles.

questions.question: Height of Tropopause at equator is
questions.explanation: Troposphere extends from surface to 16-18 km at equator due to rising hot convection currents.

questions.question: Height of Tropopause at Poles is
questions.explanation: At poles, tropopause height is 8-10 km due to lower surface temperatures.

questions.question: Higher the surface temperature, ______ would be the tropopause
questions.explanation: Warmer the surface, higher is the height of the tropopause.

questions.question: Height of tropopause
questions.explanation: Tropopause height varies with latitude, season, land-sea distribution, and synoptic situation.

questions.question: Above 8 km the lower temperatures are over
questions.explanation: Above 8 km, there is reversal of temperature and density; poles become warmer than equator.

questions.question: Atmosphere is heated by
questions.explanation: Atmosphere is heated from below by conduction, convection, radiation and latent heat release.

questions.question: The temperature at 80 km is
questions.explanation: At mesopause (80 km), temperature is about -100°C (173.15 K), the coldest area of atmosphere.

questions.question: CO2 and H2O are also called
questions.explanation: Water vapour, CO2, O3, Methane are Green House Gases that cause greenhouse effect.

questions.question: Troposphere is generally
questions.explanation: Troposphere is generally unstable due to turbulent mixing and all weather occurs here.

questions.question: Stratosphere is
questions.explanation: Stratosphere is stable due to temperature inversion caused by ozone absorption of UV radiation.

questions.question: Tropopause is discontinuous at about
questions.explanation: Tropopause has breaks/folds at about 40° Lat and 60° Lat, with 40° Lat being more prominent.

questions.question: Most of atmospheric mass is contained in
questions.explanation: About 75% of atmospheric mass and 99% of water vapour and aerosols lie within troposphere.

questions.question: Stratosphere extends from Tropopause to
questions.explanation: Stratosphere extends up to a height of 50 km from earth's surface.

questions.question: The middle atmosphere layer with temperature inversion and stability is
questions.explanation: Stratosphere has temperature inversion due to ozone absorption of UV radiation.

questions.question: Mother of Pearl clouds occur in
questions.explanation: Nacreous Clouds or Mother of Pearl Clouds are seen in upper stratosphere in higher latitudes in winters.

questions.question: The temperature in ISA at 17 km is
questions.explanation: In ISA, temperature is -56.5°C from 11 to 20 km.

questions.question: By weight, approximate ratio of O2 to N2 in the atmosphere is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen:Oxygen ratio by weight is 3:1, so O2:N2 is 1:3.

questions.question: By volume, the approximate ratio of O2 to N2 in the atmosphere is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen:Oxygen ratio by volume is 4:1, so O2:N2 is 1:4.

questions.question: By volume, the proportion of CO2 in the atmosphere is
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is 0.035% by volume in the atmosphere.

questions.question: In ISA, the mean sea level temperature is
questions.explanation: ISA mean sea level temperature is 15°C (288.15 K).

questions.question: Maximum concentration of ozone is at a height of
questions.explanation: Appreciable O3 is found between 10 and 50 km, with maximum concentration at 20-25 km.

questions.question: Additional oxygen is needed while flying above
questions.explanation: Due to rapid reduction of gases with height, supplementary Oxygen is needed above 10,000 ft.

questions.question: CO2 and H2O keep the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Green House Gases cause greenhouse effect and keep earth warmer than it would have been otherwise.

questions.question: Noctilucent clouds occur in
questions.explanation: Noctilucent Clouds are seen in the upper Mesosphere, in Polar regions.

questions.question: Nacreous clouds occur in
questions.explanation: Nacreous Clouds form in the upper Stratosphere.

questions.question: In actual atmosphere temp. at 19 km is -60°C. Find the ISA deviation?
questions.explanation: ISA temp at 19 km is -56.5°C. ISA Deviation = Actual - ISA = -60 - (-56.5) = -3.5°C

questions.question: Temperature at 2 km is 05°C what is ISA deviation?
questions.explanation: ISA temp at 2 km = 15 - (2 × 6.5) = 2°C. ISA Deviation = 5 - 2 = 3°C (approximately 5°C)

questions.question: Pressure at MSL is 1002.25 hPa. Find the ISA deviation
questions.explanation: ISA MSL pressure is 1013.25 hPa. ISA Deviation = 1002.25 - 1013.25 = -11 hPa

questions.question: The atmosphere up to 80 km has a nearly similar composition and is called the Homosphere. This composition is due to
questions.explanation: Due to earth gravitation, atmosphere up to 80 km is well mixed and has nearly similar composition.

questions.question: Half of the atmospheric air mass is contained below
questions.explanation: About 50% of atmospheric mass is below 20,000 ft (6 km).

questions.question: In jet standard atmosphere the Lapse Rate is
questions.explanation: Jet Standard Atmosphere has lapse rate of 2°C/1000 ft up to 32 km.

questions.question: The rate of fall of temperatures with height is called
questions.explanation: Lapse Rate denotes decrease of temperature with height.

questions.question: In actual atmosphere the lapse rate could
questions.explanation: In actual atmosphere, lapse rate may have any value - super adiabatic, DALR, negative (inversion), or isothermal.

questions.question: Tropical Tropopause extends from the equator to Lat. 35°-40°. Over India it is at
questions.explanation: Over India, Tropical Tropopause is found at about 16-16.5 km.

questions.question: Lapse rate in the troposphere is produced by ______ and in the stratosphere by ______
questions.explanation: Troposphere heated by terrestrial radiation from earth; Stratosphere heated by solar radiation absorbed by ozone.

questions.question: Most of the water vapour in the atmosphere is confined up to
questions.explanation: Most water vapour is confined to lower troposphere, decreasing rapidly with height.

questions.question: Negative lapse rate of temperature is
questions.explanation: Negative lapse rate means temperature increases with height (inversion).

questions.question: In ICAO ISA the atmosphere is assumed to be isothermal
questions.explanation: ISA assumes isothermal conditions from 11 to 20 km in lower stratosphere.

questions.question: One of the characteristics of our atmosphere is

options.b: Poor conductor of heat and electricity

questions.explanation: Atmosphere is a poor conductor of heat and electricity.

questions.question: Heat transfer in the atmosphere is maximum due to
questions.explanation: Convection is the most important process of heat transfer in the atmosphere.

questions.question: The knowledge of the height of tropopause is important for a pilot because

options.a: Clouds rarely reach up to this height
options.b: Weather is mainly confined up to this level

questions.explanation: Weather is mainly confined up to tropopause level; it is the maximum height to which clouds may reach.

questions.question: In ISA atmosphere the tropopause occurs at a height of
questions.explanation: ISA tropopause occurs at 11 km (36,090 ft).

questions.question: Most of the transfer of heat in the atmosphere is due to
questions.explanation: Radiation plays a significant role in heat transfer in the atmosphere.

questions.question: There is reversal of temperature in the atmosphere at 8 km because

options.a: Lapse rate at poles is always greater
options.b: Lapse rate reverses at poles and becomes negative
options.c: Lapse rate at equator is same as at poles

questions.explanation: Above 8 km, poles start warming up and become warmer than equator due to reversal of temperature.

questions.question: Low pressure area is associated with
questions.explanation: Low pressure is associated with upward motion, convergence, and bad weather.

questions.question: Winds in a low pressure area
questions.explanation: Winds converge towards low pressure center in anticlockwise direction in N hemisphere.

questions.question: In a high pressure area winds are
questions.explanation: In high pressure areas, winds are generally weak and diverge outwards.

questions.question: Flying from Low to High an altimeter would read
questions.explanation: Flying from Low to High pressure, altimeter under reads (L-H-L rule).

questions.question: Isallobars are lines of equal
questions.explanation: Isallobars are lines joining places of equal pressure change.

questions.question: What kind of a barometer is an altimeter
questions.explanation: Altimeter is an aneroid barometer with scale graduated to read altitude.

questions.question: A region between two Lows and Two Highs is
questions.explanation: Col is a region enclosed between two highs and two lows with light variable winds.

questions.question: Bad weather and better visibility is associated with
questions.explanation: Low pressure is associated with bad weather and better visibility.

questions.question: Altimeter always measures the height of aircraft above

options.c: datum at which its sub-scale is set

questions.explanation: Altimeter measures height above the datum at which its sub-scale is set.

questions.question: Two aircraft flying at same indicated altitude with altimeters set to 1013.2 hPa. One is flying over cold air mass and other over warm air mass. Which of the two has greater altitude?

options.a: AC flying over warm air mass
options.b: AC flying over cold air mass

questions.explanation: AC flying over cold air mass has greater true altitude as altimeter over reads in cold air.

questions.question: The rate of fall of pressure with height in a warm air mass compared to cold air mass will be
questions.explanation: Pressure falls at a slower pace over warm air than over cold air.

questions.question: An increase of 1000 ft at MSL is associated with decrease of pressure of
questions.explanation: Approximately 1 hPa per 30 ft, so 1000 ft ≈ 33 hPa.

questions.question: Lines drawn through places of equal pressure are known as
questions.explanation: Isobars are lines joining places of equal pressure.

questions.question: Which is true?

options.b: At trough winds back in N-hemisphere
options.c: At trough winds veer in N-hemisphere

questions.explanation: At a trough, winds back in N-hemisphere.

questions.question: Semi diurnal pressure changes are most pronounced in
questions.explanation: Semi diurnal pressure variations are large (3-5 hPa) at Equator/Tropics.

questions.question: Flying from Delhi to Kolkata at constant indicated altitude but experiencing drift to Starboard. The actual altitude will be (vis-à-vis) indicated altitude
questions.explanation: Starboard drift means wind from port. In N hemisphere, port drift means AC moving from L to H, altimeter under reads, actual altitude is lower.

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, around a Low Pressure Area wind blows
questions.explanation: In S hemisphere, winds blow clockwise around a low pressure area.

questions.question: Altimeter of AC on ground reads aerodrome elevation; its sub-scale is set to
questions.explanation: When QNH is set, altimeter indicates station elevation.

questions.question: Instrument for recording pressure is called
questions.explanation: Barometer is used for measuring/recording pressure.

questions.question: Poor visibility is associated with
questions.explanation: High pressure is associated with subsidence and poor visibility.

questions.question: On either side, perpendicular to the ______ pressures rise
questions.explanation: Pressure along a trough is lower than on either side.

questions.question: Fall of pressure with height is more rapid in
questions.explanation: Pressure falls at a faster pace over cold air than warm air.

questions.question: 300 hPa in ISA corresponds to the level
questions.explanation: 300 hPa corresponds to 30,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 18,000 ft height in ISA corresponds to the pressure level
questions.explanation: 500 hPa corresponds to 18,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 200 hPa in ISA corresponds to the level
questions.explanation: 200 hPa corresponds to 38,000-40,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 24,000 ft height in ISA corresponds to pressure level
questions.explanation: 400 hPa corresponds to 24,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 700 hPa in ISA corresponds to the Flight level
questions.explanation: 700 hPa corresponds to 10,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 40,000 ft height in ISA approximately corresponds to pressure level
questions.explanation: 200 hPa corresponds to about 38,000-40,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: 850 hPa in ISA corresponds to the height
questions.explanation: 850 hPa corresponds to 5,000 ft in ISA.

questions.question: Atmospheric pressure is due to
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is due to weight of the air column above, which is due to gravity.

questions.question: An aircraft is gaining altitude, in spite of altimeter reading constant altitude. Why?
questions.explanation: Flying towards Low pressure, altimeter over reads, so AC actually gains altitude while altimeter shows constant.

questions.question: Steep pressure gradient would mean

options.c: Isobars closely packed and strong wind

questions.explanation: Steep pressure gradient means isobars closely packed and strong winds.

questions.question: A contour of 9160 m can be expected on a constant pressure chart for pressure level
questions.explanation: 300 hPa level has contours around 9000-9500 m.

questions.question: In contour chart of 300 hPa, isohypse (contours) are drawn at interval of
questions.explanation: Contours are drawn at 80 gpm interval in 300 hPa and 200 hPa level charts.

questions.question: In constant pressure chart of 500 hPa, isohypse are drawn at interval of
questions.explanation: Contours are drawn at 40 gpm interval in 700 hPa and 500 hPa level charts.

questions.question: QNH of an aerodrome 160 m AMSL is 1005 hPa. QFE? Assuming 1 hPa = 8m
What type of inversion occurs when a stable layer lies in a high pressure area
questions.explanation: Subsidence inversion occurs in high pressure areas due to descending air.

questions.question: Which of the following would cause true altitude to increase when altimeter indicates constant altitude?
questions.explanation: In cold air, altimeter over reads, so true altitude is higher than indicated.

questions.question: The movement of wind in relation to a cyclone is
questions.explanation: In a cyclone, air ascends and converges.

questions.question: An aerodrome is at the mean sea level. Its QNH is 1014.0 hPa. Its QFF will be
questions.explanation: At MSL, QNH equals QFF (both are station pressure reduced to MSL).

questions.question: Diurnal variation of temperature is greatest when wind is
questions.explanation: Diurnal variation is maximum when wind is calm.

questions.question: Diurnal variation of temperature is maximum over
questions.explanation: Diurnal temperature variation is much larger over land than over sea.

questions.question: On a clear day the amount of solar radiation received by earth surface is
questions.explanation: In clear weather about 5/6 of solar radiation reaches earth surface.

questions.question: ALBEDO is
questions.explanation: Albedo is the reflecting power of earth (30% of solar radiation reflected back).

questions.question: During Day the ambient temperature is ______ than ground
questions.explanation: During day, ground is heated more than air, so ambient temperature is lower than ground temperature.

questions.question: Diurnal variation of temperature over ocean is
questions.explanation: Sea surface temperature shows variation of less than 1°C from day to night.

questions.question: At a coastal station the diurnal variation of temperature depends on
questions.explanation: At coastal stations, diurnal variation depends on wind direction (off-sea or off-land).

questions.question: Snow surface reflects about ______% of solar radiation
questions.explanation: Snow surface reflects about 80% of incident energy.

questions.question: Amount of Solar radiation received per unit area is
questions.explanation: Insolation is the total amount of solar radiation received per unit area.

questions.question: Solar radiation received by the earth is
questions.explanation: Solar radiation is short wave radiation.

questions.question: Rise in temperature of a surface is ______ proportional to its specific heat
questions.explanation: Rise in temperature is inversely proportional to specific heat.

questions.question: Specific heat of land is ______ than that of water
questions.explanation: Specific heat of land (0.2) is lower than water (1.0).

questions.question: Cloudy nights are
questions.explanation: Cloudy nights are warmer as clouds absorb outgoing terrestrial radiation.

questions.question: Minimum temperature is reached at
questions.explanation: Minimum temperature occurs 1/2 to 1 hour after sunrise.

questions.question: An air parcel is lifted till it gets saturated. The temperature attained by it is called
questions.explanation: Wet bulb temperature is the lowest temperature air would attain by evaporating water into it to saturate it.

questions.question: Water vapour is transparent to terrestrial radiation
questions.explanation: Water vapour partially absorbs terrestrial (long wave) radiation.

questions.question: Higher the temperature ______ would be the wavelength of emitted radiation
questions.explanation: Wien's Law: Higher temperature means shorter wavelength of maximum intensity.

questions.question: Air is a bad conductor of heat. A parcel of air can therefore be regarded as insulated from the environment
questions.explanation: Air is a bad conductor, so air parcels can be considered insulated (adiabatic process).

questions.question: Warmer the earth ______ will be the Nocturnal radiation
questions.explanation: Warmer earth emits more intense nocturnal radiation.

questions.question: Heat is the ______ of the KE of all the molecules and atoms of a substance
questions.explanation: Heat is the sum total of kinetic energy of all molecules.

questions.question: The solar radiation consists of about 46%
questions.explanation: Solar radiation consists of IR 46%, Visible 45%, UV 09%.

questions.question: The total energy radiated by a black body is proportional to its temperature (T)
questions.explanation: Stefan Boltzmann's Law: Energy radiated is proportional to T4.

questions.question: Intense radiation emitted by
questions.explanation: Hot bodies emit intense radiation (sun emits short waves).

questions.question: The wavelength of most intense radiation is inversely proportional to
questions.explanation: Wien's Law: Wavelength of most intense radiation is inversely proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.question: Hot bodies (like Sun) radiate
questions.explanation: Hot bodies radiate short waves; colder bodies radiate long waves.

questions.question: The flow of heat from earth surface is 77% by
questions.explanation: About 77% of heat flow from earth surface is by sensible heat (conduction, convection, radiation).

questions.question: -40°C = -40°F
questions.explanation: -40°C = -40°F is the only point where Celsius and Fahrenheit are equal.

questions.question: Surface Temperature is recorded at a height of
questions.explanation: Surface temperature is recorded at 1.25 m (4 ft) above ground in shade.

questions.question: The door of Stevenson's screen should open
questions.explanation: Stevenson's screen door opens opposite to sun (away from sun) to avoid direct radiation.

questions.question: The liquid used in Minimum Thermometer is
questions.explanation: Minimum thermometer uses alcohol (with dumbbell shaped iron index).

questions.question: Freezing point of water is
questions.explanation: Freezing point of water is 32°F (0°C, 273 K).

questions.question: Boiling point of water is
questions.explanation: Boiling point of water is 212°F (100°C, 373 K).

questions.question: Freezing point of water is
questions.explanation: Freezing point of water is 273 K (0°C).

questions.question: Boiling point of water is
questions.explanation: Boiling point of water is 373 K (100°C).

questions.question: Convert 68°F into Kelvin temperature
Diurnal variation of temperature is least on a day when it is
questions.explanation: Cloudy days have least diurnal variation.

questions.question: A clear and calm night is cooler than a cloudy night, because nocturnal radiation

options.b: Are partly radiated back by clouds to earth

questions.explanation: Clouds absorb and re-radiate terrestrial radiation back to earth, warming the surface.

questions.question: Which surface will cause higher diurnal variation
questions.explanation: Desert has highest diurnal variation due to low specific heat and lack of moisture.

questions.question: If temperature does not change in a layer with height on a day, indicates
questions.explanation: No change in temperature with height indicates isothermal layer.

questions.question: Density is ______ at poles than equator
questions.explanation: Density is higher at poles than equator due to lower temperatures.

questions.question: Above 8 km density is ______ at poles than at equator
questions.explanation: Above 8 km, reversal occurs and density becomes more near equator than at poles.

questions.question: The altitude in ISA at which air density is the same as the observed density is
questions.explanation: Density altitude is the altitude in ISA at which a given density occurs.

questions.question: Density is usually expressed as
questions.explanation: Density is expressed as kg/m³ or g/m³.

questions.question: Higher density altitude means
questions.explanation: Higher density altitude means taking off from airfield at higher altitude.

questions.question: For given pressure and temperature moist air has density
questions.explanation: Moist air is less dense than dry air under same conditions.

questions.question: Air is less denser in
questions.explanation: Air is less dense at high altitudes, in warm air, and high humidity - all of these.

questions.question: Density altitude may define

options.a: The altitude at which the prevailing pressure occurs
options.b: The altitude in ISA at which the prevailing density occurs
options.c: The altitude in actual atmosphere at which the prevailing density occurs

questions.explanation: Density altitude is the altitude in ISA at which the prevailing density occurs.

questions.question: Temperature being constant, if pressure increases the density altitude
questions.explanation: If pressure increases at constant temperature, density altitude lowers.

questions.question: For every 1°C change in temperature, density altitude differs from pressure altitude by
questions.explanation: 1°C temperature deviation from ISA equals 120 ft density altitude.

questions.question: The ratio in % between the amount of water vapour present in the air to the amount of water vapour that it can hold at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: Relative humidity is the ratio of actual water vapour to maximum possible at same temperature.

questions.question: The temperature to which air be cooled at constant pressure to become saturated is called
questions.explanation: Dew point temperature is the temperature to which air must be cooled to become saturated.

questions.question: Free air temperature, Wet bulb temperature and Dew point temperature are equal when
questions.explanation: When RH is 100%, T = Tw = Td.

questions.question: On a rainy day compared to sunny day the length of runway required is
questions.explanation: On rainy day, higher humidity means lower density, so longer runway required.

questions.question: The spread (difference) between Free air temperature and Dew point temperature is ______ when air is saturated
questions.explanation: When saturated, T = Td, so spread is zero (least).

questions.question: The saturation vapour pressure over water is ______ than the ice
questions.explanation: Saturation vapour pressure over water is more than over ice.

questions.question: As the temperature of the air increases, the amount of water vapour required to saturate it
questions.explanation: Warmer air can hold more water vapour, so amount required to saturate increases.

questions.question: The actual amount of water vapour contained in a given volume of air at a given temperature is termed as
questions.explanation: Absolute humidity is the actual amount of water vapour in a given volume of air.

questions.question: Humidity Mixing Ratio ______ when air is lifted adiabatically
questions.explanation: HMR remains constant when air is lifted adiabatically (no addition or removal of water vapour).

questions.question: It is the lowest temperature which air would attain by evaporating water into it to saturate it
questions.explanation: Wet bulb temperature is the lowest temperature air would attain by evaporating water into it to saturate it.

questions.question: In S hemisphere if an observer faces wind, low will be to his
questions.explanation: In S hemisphere, with back to wind, low is to the right (opposite of N hemisphere).

questions.question: In N hemisphere due to rotation of earth winds are deflected to
questions.explanation: Coriolis force deflects winds to the right in N hemisphere.

questions.question: Local Winds follow Buys Ballots law
questions.explanation: Local winds (land/sea breeze, anabatic, etc.) do not follow Buys Ballot's law.

questions.question: Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the ______ of wind direction in N hemisphere
questions.explanation: Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the right of wind direction in N hemisphere.

questions.question: Geostrophic wind is due to the balance between the forces
questions.explanation: Geostrophic wind is balance between pressure gradient force and Coriolis force.

questions.question: Coriolis force is strongest at
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is maximum at poles (sin 90° = 1) and minimum at equator.

questions.question: Geostrophic rule breaks down at
questions.explanation: At equator, Coriolis force is zero, so geostrophic formula breaks down.

questions.question: Fohn winds are
questions.explanation: Fohn winds are warm and dry downslope winds on leeward side of mountains.

questions.question: The wind sliding down a hill during night is called
questions.explanation: Katabatic wind is downslope cold wind due to nocturnal cooling.

questions.question: With the onset of sea breeze there is a ______ in temperature and ______ in RH
questions.explanation: Sea breeze brings fall in temperature and increase in humidity (RH).

questions.question: Sea breeze sets in by ______ and dies off at ______
questions.explanation: Sea breeze sets in during day and dies off at night.

questions.question: If an aircraft in N-hemisphere flies from H to L it will experience
questions.explanation: Flying from H to L in N hemisphere, wind is from starboard (right), causing port drift.

questions.question: In N-Hemisphere if you experience Port drift, altimeter will read
questions.explanation: Port drift means wind from starboard, AC moving from L to H, altimeter under reads.

questions.question: Lines of constant wind speed drawn on weather charts are called
questions.explanation: Isotachs are lines of constant wind speed.

questions.question: Squall are distinguished from gusts by
questions.explanation: Squall lasts longer than gust (gust is transient, squall lasts for 1 minute or more).

questions.question: The thermal wind is

options.a: The wind that blows because of thermals
options.b: The warm wind that blows down the hill on the leeward side
options.c: The wind which must be added vectorially to the lower level geostrophic wind to obtain the upper level geostrophic wind

questions.explanation: Thermal wind is the vector difference between upper and lower level geostrophic winds.

questions.question: On a weather map if isobars are closely packed, the surface winds are likely to be

options.c: Strong and blowing across the isobars

questions.explanation: Closely packed isobars mean steep pressure gradient, hence strong winds parallel to isobars.

questions.question: Anabatic wind occurs

options.b: Any time of day and night

questions.explanation: Anabatic winds are upslope winds that occur during day due to solar heating.

questions.question: Anabatic wind is stronger than katabatic
questions.explanation: Anabatic (daytime upslope) winds are generally stronger than katabatic winds.

questions.question: Katabatic wind is down slope cold wind due to nocturnal cooling
questions.explanation: Katabatic wind is downslope cold wind due to nocturnal cooling.

questions.question: Katabatic wind occur due to sinking of cold air down the hill slope
questions.explanation: Katabatic winds occur due to sinking of cold, dense air down the hill slope.

questions.question: Anabatic wind occur due to downward movement of air along valley
questions.explanation: Anabatic wind is upward movement of air along valley slopes.

questions.question: Sea breeze is stronger than land breeze
questions.explanation: Sea breeze is stronger and more regular than land breeze.

questions.question: The wind blows clockwise around a low in N-hemisphere
questions.explanation: In N hemisphere, wind blows anticlockwise around a low.

questions.question: The wind blows clockwise around a low in S-hemisphere
questions.explanation: In S hemisphere, wind blows clockwise around a low.

questions.question: The wind blows anticlockwise around a low in N-hemisphere
questions.explanation: In N hemisphere, wind blows anticlockwise around a low.

questions.question: The wind blows anticlockwise around a low in S-hemisphere
questions.explanation: In S hemisphere, wind blows clockwise around a low.

questions.question: The resultant wind that blows under the influence of pressure gradient force, geostrophic force and cyclostrophic force is called
questions.explanation: Gradient wind is balance of pressure gradient, Coriolis, and centripetal forces.

questions.question: Due to friction, from day to night for an isobaric pattern (in N hemisphere) the surface wind backs and weakens
questions.explanation: At night, friction layer shrinks, wind backs and weakens.

questions.question: The winds which spirals inward counter-clockwise in the N Hemisphere are associated with
questions.explanation: Winds spiral inward counter-clockwise around a low in N hemisphere.

questions.question: Lower level wind 05010 kt, upper level wind 23005 kt, what is the thermal wind
questions.explanation: Thermal wind = Upper - Lower = 23005 - 05010 = 05005 kt (vector subtraction).

questions.question: A change in wind direction from 310° to 020° is
questions.explanation: Change from 310° to 020° is clockwise, hence veering.

questions.question: A change from 270° to 250° is
questions.explanation: Change from 270° to 250° is anticlockwise, hence backing.

questions.question: Sudden changes in wind speed from 10 kt to 30 kt and then to 15 kt are
questions.explanation: Transient increase in wind speed is a gust.

questions.question: Sudden change in wind speed from 10 kt to 30 kt for 2-3 minutes
questions.explanation: Squall is sudden increase in wind speed by 16 kt or more, lasting for 1 minute or more.

questions.question: A significant wind shear is generally associated with TS or line squall
questions.explanation: Significant wind shear is associated with TS or line squall.

questions.question: Cyclostrophic wind gives a good approximation of the wind in an intense tropical storm
questions.explanation: Cyclostrophic wind gives good approximation near center of tropical storm.

questions.question: Rotor clouds have extremely turbulent flying conditions
questions.explanation: Rotor clouds have extremely turbulent flying conditions.

questions.question: Friction causes winds to flow cross isobaric by ______ over land and ______ over sea
questions.explanation: Over land, wind crosses isobars at about 30°; over sea, about 15°.

questions.question: If the S is warmer than the N, level by level, from surface up to higher levels, then the ______ wind will strengthen with height with no change in direction in N hemisphere
questions.explanation: Thermal wind is westerly when S is warmer than N.

questions.question: Gradient wind is ______ of the geostrophic wind in an anticyclone
questions.explanation: Gradient wind is super geostrophic in an anticyclone.

questions.question: Gale is

options.a: Persistent strong winds exceeding 33 kt, associated with depression
options.b: Persistent strong winds with mean speed 44 kt, associated with thunderstorm
options.c: Marked increase in wind speed lasting few minutes associated with CB or DS

questions.explanation: Gale is persistent mean wind of speed 34 kt or more, associated with depressions.

questions.question: In N hemisphere thermal wind is parallel to
